evidence.excerpt: A two-dimensional finite-difference model was developed to simulate transient heat and moisture transfer in a sealed steel enclosure containing a heat-dissipating printed circuit board. The model couples Fourier conduction through the walls with Fickian vapour diffusion and accounts for condensation on internal surfaces when local temperature drops below the dew point. Internal heat generation was set at 5 W, representing a typical low-power controller unit. Simulations were run for a 24-hour diurnal ambient profile representative of a Pannonian autumn day. Results showed that condensation first occurred on the lower half of the front panel after approximately 17 minutes of rapid external temperature drop at −1.2 °C/min. Increasing the initial internal air volume by 30 % by deepening the enclosure reduced condensation onset time by only 4 minutes, while adding a 2-g silica-gel desiccant delayed onset by 38 minutes. The model was validated against thermocouple and humidity logger measurements from a physical enclosure subjected to a controlled temperature ramp in a climate chamber.
